title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
slides: Who's really behind AI's new scraping opt-out?
Big names back a standard to let sites refuse bots
But it only works if scrapers actually honor it
Publishers now have a lever—though enforcement stays fuzzy
Ask your vendors if they respect the signal
thread_text:
1. The opt-out nobody checks

A new standard lets sites tell AI bots to back off. Big names are backing it—but compliance is voluntary.

2. Big names, soft power

Major publishers and tech firms announced support for the signal. There's no enforcement mechanism, just good faith.

3. Honor system 2.0

Scrapers can ignore the signal without penalty. The standard only works if everyone plays nice—and AI companies have little incentive.

4. Leverage without teeth

Publishers finally have a formal way to refuse bots. But without audits or penalties, it's a lever made of cardboard.

5. Ask your vendor today

Does your AI tool respect scraping opt-outs? If they can't answer, that's your answer. Test one vendor this week.
